entities.summary: Guillaume Fillastre, sometimes called the Elder, was a French cardinal, canonist, humanist, and geographer. He was born in 1382 and died on November 15, 1428. Fillastre was a prominent figure in the Catholic Church, serving as a cardinal and a diplomat. He was also a scholar and a writer, producing works on theology, canon law, and geography. His most famous work is the 'Libellus de parte Marcelli', a treatise on the nature of the sea. Fillastre's contributions to the Church and his scholarly works had a lasting impact on the development of Catholic theology and canon law. He was also a key figure in the negotiations between the Church and the French monarchy. In 1428, Fillastre was appointed as the Bishop of Bayeux, a position he held until his death. His legacy as a scholar, diplomat, and Church leader continues to be studied and admired by historians today.
